
# This script is used to perform quality control and filtering of the hMSC dataset using Seurat package.

# --- START OF USER CONFIGURATION ---
# Please modify the following paths according to your system environment.

# Full path to the gene count matrix file generated by the previous script.
file_input <- "/path/to/your/project/output/txi_kallisto_tsv_count.txt"

# Root directory for all analysis outputs.
dir_output <- "/path/to/your/project/output"
# --- END OF USER CONFIGURATION ---

rm(list = ls(all = TRUE))
ls()

library(Seurat)
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2)

setwd(dir_output)
cat("Current working directory:", getwd(), "\n")

# Create a subdirectory for this script's outputs
qc_dir <- file.path(dir_output, "01_SeuratQC")
if (!dir.exists(qc_dir)) {
  dir.create(qc_dir)
}

# Setup the Seurat Object
# Load the hMSC dataset
rt <- read.table(file = file_input, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)
rt <- as.matrix(rt)
rownames(rt) <- rt[, 1]
hMSC.data <- rt[, 2:ncol(rt)]

# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
hMSC <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = hMSC.data)
hMSC

# Standard pre-processing workflow
# QC and selecting cells for further analysis

# The [[ operator can add columns to object metadata. This is a great place to stash QC stats
hMSC[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(hMSC, pattern = "^MT-")

# Show QC metrics for the first 5 cells
head(hMSC@meta.data, 5)

# Visualize QC metrics as a violin plot
pdf(file = "01_SeuratQC/QCBefore.pdf", width = 10, height = 7)
VlnPlot(hMSC, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
dev.off()

# We filter cells that have unique genes detected number over 15000 or less than 5000
# We filter cells that have total number of molecules detected over 1200000 or less than 500000
# We filter cells that have >5% mitochondrial counts
# Now, 95 A, 93 G, 68 O left
hMSC <- subset(hMSC, subset = nFeature_RNA > 5000 & nFeature_RNA < 15000 & nCount_RNA > 500000 & nCount_RNA < 1200000 & percent.mt < 5)

pdf(file = "01_SeuratQC/QCAfter.pdf", width = 10, height = 7)
VlnPlot(hMSC, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"), ncol = 3)
dev.off()

# Normalize and run dimensionality reduction on control dataset
# Identification of highly variable features (feature selection)
# Scaling the data
hMSC <- SCTransform(hMSC, verbose = FALSE)

# Identify the 10 most highly variable genes
top10 <- head(VariableFeatures(hMSC), 10)

# plot variable features with and without labels
plot1 <- VariableFeaturePlot(hMSC)
plot2 <- LabelPoints(plot = plot1, points = top10, repel = TRUE)

pdf(file = "01_SeuratQC/VariableFeature.pdf", width = 14, height = 7)
plot1 + plot2
dev.off()

# Perform linear dimensional reduction
hMSC <- RunPCA(hMSC, npcs = 30, features = VariableFeatures(object = hMSC), verbose = FALSE)

# Examine and visualize PCA results a few different ways
print(hMSC[["pca"]], dims = 1:5, nfeatures = 5)
VizDimLoadings(hMSC, dims = 1:2, reduction = "pca")
DimPlot(hMSC, reduction = "pca")
DimHeatmap(hMSC, dims = 1:2, cells = 250, balanced = TRUE)

# Cluster the cells
hMSC <- FindNeighbors(hMSC, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
hMSC <- FindClusters(hMSC, resolution = 0.7, verbose = FALSE)

# Look at cluster IDs of the first 5 cells
head(Idents(hMSC), 5)

# Run non-linear dimensional reduction (UMAP/tSNE)
# If you haven't installed UMAP, you can do so via reticulate::py_install(packages = 'umap-learn')
hMSC <- RunUMAP(hMSC, dims = 1:30)

# Visualize the UMAP
DimPlot(hMSC, reduction = "umap")

# Save the Seurat object and the data matrix
hMSC@meta.data$medium <- NULL
hMSC@meta.data$cell_type <- NULL

hMSC@meta.data$medium[hMSC@meta.data$orig.ident == "A"] <- "1-d AM"
hMSC@meta.data$medium[hMSC@meta.data$orig.ident == "G"] <- "GM"
hMSC@meta.data$medium[hMSC@meta.data$orig.ident == "O"] <- "1-d OM"

# Save the Seurat object and the data matrix
hMSC.data.filter <- as.matrix(hMSC.data[, colnames(hMSC@assays$RNA)])
hMSC.data.num <- matrix(as.numeric(hMSC.data.filter), ncol = ncol(hMSC.data.filter))
dimnames(hMSC.data.num) <- list(rownames(hMSC.data.filter), colnames(hMSC.data.filter))

saveRDS(hMSC, file = paste0(dir_output, "/01_SeuratQC/hMSC.rds"))
save(hMSC.data, hMSC.data.num, file = paste0(dir_output, "/01_SeuratQC/hMSC.Seurat.Rdata"))
